newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal pilots to resume selective strike.
newsitem.headline: Portugal pilots to resume selective strike.

text.p: Pilots at struggling Portuguese state airline TAP-Air Portugal have agreed to resume a selective strike indefinitely from Saturday after talks with management over working hours failed.
"The decision to maintain the stoppages of non-scheduled flights was approved by the great majority of pilots," Angelo Felgueiras, vice-president of the pilots' union, told reporters.
He said 257 pilots voted at a general assembly on Thursday night to continue the strike, 15 voted against and 10 abstained.
From midnight local time (2300 GMT Friday), pilots will refuse to operate flights not scheduled at least three days in advance in a protest against the inefficient organisation of their hours.
"TAP deeply regrets the incomprehensible intransigence of the pilots' union," a statement said.

"The decision to maintain the strike represents a very serious attitude, given the numerous proposals, efforts and appeals to good sense put forward by the management representing TAP's 7,500 workers," it added.
TAP said it was determined to continue talks with the Civil Aviation Pilots' Union (SPAC), which represents all of TAP's 430 pilots, to seek an end to the dispute.

Two weekends ago, twelve TAP flights were cancelled, stranding at least 1,300 people. Pilots then suspended the strike until 2300 GMT on Friday to continue talks with TAP management and government officials.
The government has warned that TAP could face heavy losses during the peak holiday season because of the strike.
TAP flies international routes and to the Portuguese mid-Atlantic islands of Madeira and the Azores.
The government had said the strike risks the survival of the airline, which hopes to return to profit in 1997 after more than two decades of losses.
TAP pilots staged a two-day strike in April in a protest against working hours, grounding international flights and stranding some 14,000 passengers.
